messages:
maria (DevEx): quick question - trying to configure the JS SDK to hit a customer's private VPC endpoint behind our corporate proxy. base URL is https://inference.internal.corp and we set base_url in the client, but auth keeps 403-ing. using SDK v1.3.1 in a container. any checklist i should run?

kevin (SDK): checklist i run for this sort of setup: 1) confirm the SDK is actually sending the API key header (Authorization: Bearer $KEY) to the custom base_url, 2) TLS: ensure the client trusts the private CA (or use NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS), 3) proxy agent: Node needs an https-proxy-agent or global-agent to route outbound requests, 4) streaming vs non-streaming: proxies sometimes break chunked responses. can you paste the tiny repro or the curl you used?

maria (DevEx): here's what i did quickly:
```bash
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk-corp-xxxx"
node -e "const R = require('@redwood/inference'); const c=new R.Client({base_url:'https://inference.internal.corp'}); c.text.generate({input:'hi'}).then(console.log).catch(e=>console.error(e));"
```
response is a 403 from the endpoint (not from proxy). TLS handshake looks OK in the logs but the server side says token missing.

alex (Platform): two quick possibilities: 1) the ingress at the private endpoint might be validating ALPN/SNI or expecting a specific Host header. Make sure base_url host matches the TLS cert SAN or set Host header accordingly. 2) If you routed through a proxy that re-writes headers, Authorization could be stripped. Check proxy policy logs.

kevin (SDK): adding actionable code snippets — Node + https-proxy-agent + custom CA:
```js
// Node example
const {Client} = require('@redwood/inference');
const HttpsProxyAgent = require('https-proxy-agent');
const fs = require('fs');

const agent = new HttpsProxyAgent(process.env.HTTPS_PROXY || 'http://proxy.corp:3128');
// if you have a private CA bundle
const ca = fs.readFileSync('/etc/ssl/certs/internal-ca.pem');

const client = new Client({
  base_url: 'https://inference.internal.corp',
  api_key: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY,
  fetchOptions: { agent, // used by node-fetch/undici under the hood
                  // pass ca if your runtime supports it via agent or NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS
                }
});

client.text.generate({input:'hello'}).then(console.log).catch(console.error);
```
For Python (requests):
```py
import os, requests
base='https://inference.internal.corp'
headers={'Authorization': f"Bearer {os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']}"}
resp = requests.post(base + '/v1/text:generate', json={'input':'hi'}, headers=headers, proxies={'https': os.environ.get('HTTPS_PROXY')}, verify='/etc/ssl/certs/internal-ca.pem')
print(resp.status_code, resp.text)
```

samir (Eng): streaming note: corporate proxies often buffer chunked responses until the upstream closes the connection. if you're trying to use the SDK streaming API (server-sent chunks) and you see no partial frames until the end, it's likely the proxy. Workarounds: a) configure the proxy to passthrough chunked transfer for that route, b) use the non-streaming endpoint with smaller max_tokens and poll, or c) consider websocket-based streaming if your proxy supports ws/wss pass-through.

maria (DevEx): good point — we are seeing full response only when stream=false. how do i force the SDK to not use SSE?

kevin (SDK): our client exposes stream: boolean on calls. set stream:false to get the full response model in one shot. Example: client.chat.completions.create({messages, stream:false}). Also increase request timeout/backoff when behind proxies (they sometimes add latency).

alex (Platform): small debugging commands:
- curl with proxy and verbose:
  HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:3128 curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://inference.internal.corp/v1/health
Look for header rewrite and TLS cert CN/SAN.
- check proxy logs for "remove-header Authorization" rules.

kevin (SDK): one more: for Docker images, add CA bundle into the image and set NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS or REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE for Python. Example Dockerfile snippet:
```dockerfile
COPY internal-ca.pem /etc/ssl/certs/internal-ca.pem
ENV NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/ssl/certs/internal-ca.pem
ENV REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/certs/internal-ca.pem
```
This avoids disabling verification. Avoid rejectUnauthorized=false in prod.

maria (DevEx): got it — will try the proxy-agent + CA bundle path and open a docs PR with the Node/Python snippets. i'll also check if the customer's ingress expects a special Host header. thanks! :tada:
